claim: A Hooke-plus-Gaussian-process static force model improves nonlinear predictive force/motion control and supports uncertainty-tightened pointwise force constraints on a rigid whiteboard, but the guarantees are conditional and do not establish safety for dynamic history-dependent soft contact.
problem_and_setting: A KUKA lightweight robot traces a sinusoidal path on a rigid whiteboard while jointly controlling motion and contact force under uncertainty in the static output map.
method_or_mechanism: A zero-mean squared-exponential GP residual augments Hooke physics. Eighty-five spaced points selected from 20,000 measurements train the hybrid model. Nonlinear path-following MPC uses a 150 ms horizon and 10 ms sampling; GP two-standard-deviation uncertainty tightens a nominal 0-6 N interval to 0.7-5.3 N.
content_summary: Hybrid model RMSE is 0.41 N versus 1.06 N linear and 0.91 N Hertz. The tightening is interpreted as about 95.45% pointwise satisfaction under assumptions. In simulation it prevents contact loss under a -1.3 Nm disturbance and yields 0.25 N force RMSE versus 0.77 N for nonlinear MPC. Hardware linear control becomes unstable, nonlinear control violates the maximum constraint, and hybrid control reports about 12% lower maximum and 14% lower average error, with all calculations below 10 ms.
synthesis_role: Closest prior for learned contact-output modeling with uncertainty-tightened constrained MPC; generic novelty for this combination is exhausted.
development_link: A soft-contact proposal must show why static-output GP uncertainty fails under relaxation, hysteresis, heterogeneity, geometry shift, and scanning history, then add only a minimal identifiable state or distinct impedance/safety mechanism under matched data and compute budgets.

evidence.finding: Hooke physics plus a GP trained on 85 points yields 0.41 N RMSE versus 1.06 N linear and 0.91 N Hertz.
A 150 ms horizon, 10 ms controller tightens 0-6 N to 0.7-5.3 N using two-standard-deviation GP uncertainty.
Recursive feasibility, convergence, and chance satisfaction require closed nonempty tightened sets and uncertainty confined to the static output map.
Untightened control loses contact during a -1.3 Nm disturbance, whereas tightening preserves simulated force bounds.
Hybrid MPC reports 0.25 N force RMSE versus 0.77 N nonlinear-model MPC.
Linear control is unstable, nonlinear control violates maximum force, and hybrid control reduces maximum and average error about 12% and 14%, with computation below 10 ms.
Online updating, moving environments, cooperation, and transfer remain unresolved, and online learning creates a priori unknown constraints.

assumptions: Stationary GP residual represents force error

reported: Online and moving-environment adaptation are unresolved
inferred: Static GP lacks path-dependent memory unless history is encoded
Pointwise chance bounds do not prove trajectory, passivity, deformation, or clinical safety
Rigid-surface RMSE does not prove soft finite-area benefit

conflicts_with: Unconditional safety from a two-sigma pointwise bound
Claims about tissue memory, finite-area pressure, passivity, or optimal impedance
